newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-ZELENSKAJA WINS DOWNHILL AS SEIZINGER CRASHES.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ZELENSKAJA WINS DOWNHILL AS SEIZINGER CRASHES.

text.p: Russian Warwara Zelenskaja eclipsed the favourites in a women's World Cup downhill on Saturday as Olympic champion Katja Seizinger crashed out.
Seizinger's exit, after a fall as she came off a jump, will have severely dented the German's hopes of defending her overall World Cup title and of taking the downhill trophy this season.
Switzerland's Heidi Zurbriggen, who had a lead of only three points over Seizinger in the downhill standings before Saturday, was able to extend the gap after joint second place in the race.

Zurbriggen, who had to share victory in Cortina d'Ampezzo last week with Italian Isolde Kostner, shared second spot this time with Austria's Renate Goetschl in a time of one minute 25.07 seconds, 0.09 seconds behind Zelenskaja.
Seizinger skied down the hill after her accident and said she would be fit to race in Sunday's slalom here, which counts with the downhill for a combined competition.
The slalom will be the last race before the world championships get underway in Sestriere, Italy, on Monday.
Germany's Miriam Vogt also fell on the tricky, technical course but like her team mate Seizinger she was unhurt.
